name: link-button
title: Link button
description: A link that looks like a button: a call to action that goes to another page.

when: A call to action that navigates: "Add product" to /products/new.

instead.when: The press changes something on this page.

builtIn: Keeps link semantics: role link and a real href that works without JavaScript.
youProvide: An `aria-label` when it shows only an icon.

genui.description: A button-styled link to another page. Use button instead when nothing navigates.

href.description: Where it goes. Rendered as a real `href`, so the link works before (and without) JavaScript.

variant.description: Button's look: `primary` for the one main call to action of a view.

iconBefore.description: Lucide icon name shown before the label.

iconAfter.description: Lucide icon name shown after the label.

LinkButton.name: suppressHydrationWarning
LinkButton.description:
A React-only flag that suppresses the warning React normally logs when an element's
server-rendered content doesn't match the client render during hydration. See [React
docs](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/client/hydrateRoot#suppressing-unavoidable-hydration-mismatch-errors).

LinkButton.name: render
LinkButton.type: (props: DetailedHTMLProps<LinkWithRequiredHref, HTMLAnchorElement> | DetailedHTMLProps<HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, HTMLSpanElement>, renderProps: LinkRenderProps) => ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>>
LinkButton.description:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Note: You can check if `'href' in props` in order to tell whether to render an `<a>` element.

Requirements:

- You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<a>` is expected, you cannot render a
  `<button>`).
- Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
- You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop
  as appropriate.

LinkButton.name: download
LinkButton.description:
Causes the browser to download the linked URL. A string may be provided to suggest a file name.
See [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#download).

LinkButton.name: hrefLang
LinkButton.description:
Hints at the human language of the linked URL.
See[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#hreflang).

LinkButton.name: ping
LinkButton.description:
A space-separated list of URLs to ping when the link is followed. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#ping).

LinkButton.name: referrerPolicy
LinkButton.description:
How much of the referrer to send when following the link. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#referrerpolicy).

LinkButton.name: iconAfter

LinkButton.name: isExternal
LinkButton.description:
Link's convention: opens in a new tab with `noopener noreferrer`, shows `arrow-up-right` after the label
(unless `iconAfter` is set) and tells screen readers it opens a new tab. With `onPress` a plain click
opens nothing (the app handles it in place), so the arrow and the new-tab words are left out; `target`
and `rel` stay for the page before JavaScript. Disabled, it opens nothing either: no `target`, `rel` or
new-tab words (the arrow stays, as `iconAfter` would).

LinkButton.name: onPress
LinkButton.description:
Optional. Runs on a plain primary click or Enter, and cancels that navigation (`preventDefault`), so the
app can handle it in place (open a dialog, track and route). A click with Ctrl, Cmd, Shift or Alt, or with
the middle button, is left to the browser (new tab, new window, download). Without JavaScript the `href`
is followed as usual. It receives the click itself, a `React.MouseEvent<HTMLAnchorElement>`, not the
`PressEvent` Button's `onPress` receives.
